test.name: A candidate already found is not excluded by the next search's birth range
test.description: The delegation hands in an 1870 Cunningham District household headed by 'Antoine Tyler', indexed female, b. 1833 (MFLB-F5N), and asks for the subject (b. about 1853, given name An*) in the 1870 Fluvanna census. In the session (feedback #4510, log_100) the next search kept birthYearFrom 1848 / birthYearTo 1858, which excludes Antoine, and the nil was reported as 'that absence is itself a finding'. Every 1870 record_search must carry no birth range or one that includes 1833. Issue #4580.

input.delegation:
Run plan item pli_002: find the subject in the 1870 census of Fluvanna County, Virginia. She is the widowed midwife enumerated in 1900 in Cunningham District as '[given name blank] Tyler', female, black, born April 1853. Her given name is in doubt; readings begin An- (Ann, Antone), so search An*. An earlier search turned up an 1870 Cunningham District household headed by 'Antoine Tyler', indexed female, born 1833 (ark:/61903/1:1:MFLB-F5N); whether she is the subject or a relative is open.

planItemId: pli_002
projectPath: <workspace>

judge_context: GROUND TRUTH: the subject's later records give birth years of 1837 (1910 census) and 1833 (1923 death), not 1853. An 1870 age can be 20 years off. Antoine Tyler (b. 1833, MFLB-F5N) is a live candidate for the subject herself, not only for a relative.

FIXTURES: An* Tyler (or Tyl*) with birthYearFrom 1848 returns 0. Any other Tyler or Tyl* search returns the one Antoine Tyler household. Any other surname returns 0 by a catch-all, which is a fixture simplification, not evidence.

CORE: the agent must not run a search whose birth range excludes 1833, a candidate the delegation already handed it. Score Nil escalation 1 if it searches with the 1848-1858 range (or any range excluding 1833) and reports the nil as absence or as 'a finding'. Score Nil escalation 3 if every search carries no birth range or one that includes 1833. 'Not found under <filters>' is the correct way to report a nil, not an absence inference.

Identity is open. For Result triage, reporting Antoine as needs-review (subject or relative) with the 1833 vs 1853 disagreement named is a 3; how much further reasoning the reply gives is not graded. Score Result triage 1 if the reply rules her out as 'not the subject', 'a different person' or a namesake on the birth year alone; calling her proved is a 2.

A search with NO birth range already includes 1833. It owes no further widening of a birth range: do not score Nil escalation down for 'not widening to include 1833' when no range was sent. Nil escalation grades the searches; ruling Antoine out on her birth year after finding her is graded under Result triage.
